facts.raw_span: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were all within normal limits
no evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses
7.0 × 6.0 × 4.2 cm tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

concepts.why: The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis with lymphovascular invasion and a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types supports the diagnosis of a mixed germ cell tumor.
The presence of a pleomorphic tumor with small, medium, and large cells and lymphovascular invasion is consistent with embryonal carcinoma, a subtype of testicular cancer.
The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis with lymphovascular invasion is consistent with yolk sac tumor, a subtype of testicular cancer.
The presence of a pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types is consistent with teratoma, a subtype of testicular cancer.

The lack of evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on the positron emission tomography–computed tomography scan rules out lymphoma as a primary diagnosis but the presence of lymphovascular invasion and a pleomorphic tumor with distinct cell types could suggest a secondary lymphomatous component.

rationales.F04: Large, solid masses in both testes are more typical of testicular tumors like Mixed Germ Cell Tumor, Embryonal Carcinoma, Yolk Sac Tumor, and Teratoma, rather than Lymphoma.
rationales.F06: No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses makes Lymphoma less likely.
rationales.F07: A large tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion is more typical of aggressive testicular tumors like Mixed Germ Cell Tumor, Embryonal Carcinoma, Yolk Sac Tumor, and Teratoma, rather than Lymphoma.
rationales.F08: A pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types is highly suggestive of Mixed Germ Cell Tumor.
